bull.b: Minimal debt reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves flexibility while Alterity advances its clinical programs. The substantial equity base and stable assets provide a stronger balance-sheet foundation than many development-stage biotechs, although future funding needs remain important.

Patent protection extending to at least 2045 could provide durable exclusivity if ATH434 is approved, improving its strategic and commercial value. It may also strengthen partnership potential and support development across MSA, Parkinson’s disease, and related disorders.

Clinically meaningful efficacy in a controlled Phase 2 study provides important validation for ATH434 and supports progression toward a pivotal Phase 3 program. MSA is also described as a rare disease with no approved treatment, creating a potentially differentiated opportunity.

bear.b: The decline to zero revenue confirms that Alterity currently lacks a dependable commercial revenue stream and remains primarily dependent on development activities. Without product sales, future progress is not yet supported by operating income and remains exposed to financing requirements.

Accelerating negative operating cash flow increases the capital required to sustain research and clinical execution. Persistent burn can shorten financial runway and make the company more dependent on external funding, particularly as it prepares to advance ATH434 toward Phase 3.

Large recurring operating and net losses show that Alterity has not yet demonstrated sustainable earnings power. Continued losses can consume equity and increase the likelihood that additional capital will be needed before any clinical asset generates commercial returns.
